claims.claim: No postsolve.gms (core or modules) touches spv/teVRE; premise is false
Searched core plus 48 module-realization postsolve.gms files
claims.note: The count is slightly wrong (there are 50 module postsolve files). The conclusion still holds.

claims.claim: core/bounds.gms:76 caps teVRE capacity (incl. spv) at 1.05*pm_histCap for 2015–2025 where data exist
modules/47_regipol/none/bounds.gms:19 caps 2025 spv vm_deltaCap at 2× the 2011–2020 maximum historical addition
claims.note: The formula is quoted correctly, but the answer leaves out two things. The bound applies only to DEU (loop regi$sameAs(regi,"DEU")). And `none` is not the default realization; the default is regiCarbonPrice, whose bounds.gms has no spv bound. So by default this bound is not active.

claims.claim: 40_techpol realizations set only lower bounds (vm_cap.lo from p40_TechBound) for spv
claims.note: The answer doesn't say that NPi2025 is the default (main.gms:364). This is a minor omission.

claims.claim: The listed bounds are the solar upper bounds in bounds.gms
claims.note: The answer misses the default-active 2025 spv generation upper bound for EUR regions (vm_prodSe.up based on historical growth rates). This is the bound the answer key highlights.

claims.claim: postsolve.gms files only compute reporting parameters and don't write .up/.lo/.fx on capacity variables
claims.note: True for capacity variables. But 'only reporting parameters' overgeneralizes: some postsolve files set bounds on other variables and update prices and taxes.

grade.went_well: The answer corrected the false premise clearly: no postsolve.gms touches spv. It backed this with a real search, and the core/bounds.gms:76 citation is accurate. It also correctly said the techpol bounds are lower bounds rather than caps.
grade.answer_key_issues: The key cites only core/bounds.gms:94. That line is a vm_prodSe (generation) upper bound for EUR regions, not a capacity bound. The capacity upper bound in core is vm_cap.up at core/bounds.gms:76, which the key leaves out.
grade.summary: The answer correctly rejects the premise: no postsolve.gms touches spv bounds. It also correctly cites the default vm_cap.up at core/bounds.gms:76. However, it presents the 2025 spv deltaCap cap from 47_regipol/none as a general bound, without saying it is DEU-only and belongs to a non-default realization (the default is regiCarbonPrice). It also misses the EUR vm_prodSe.up for spv at core/bounds.gms:94.
